methodology.summary: Each turn runs the production orchestrator pipeline against a live Workers AI model. Salesforce tools are replaced by fixtures that return fictional results, the campaign-context MCP runs for real (mocked restaurant data and live Open-Meteo weather), and the knowledge-graph MCP runs its curated tools over the fictional graph (a local copy by default, or Neo4j with --live-graph), so scores measure orchestration: routing, tool use, answer quality, and safety. They do not measure Salesforce agent quality. Each demo scenario also has a written rubric: deterministic criteria plus 1-5 quality ratings from a cross-family judge panel, summarized as a 0-100 Quality Index with a 95% confidence interval. Every turn is priced at Cloudflare's Workers AI list rates.
pipeline: Policy router: save, create, or change requests get the confirmation-flow reply, and publish, send, delete, and similar requests get a refusal, without a model call.

Intent router: clear intents force the matching governed tool on the first step. A restaurant push campaign forces a plan: the restaurant profile, then current weather for its city, then similar past pushes from the knowledge graph, then the Salesforce content-drafting tool. Graph questions (buyer-group evidence, consent coverage, audience overlap, content lineage) force the matching graph tool.

Model: the production system prompt (concise Markdown allowed), 11 autonomous Salesforce tools with Hosted MCP names and descriptions, the two campaign-context tools, six knowledge-graph tools, up to six steps, a 4,096-token output limit, and the 150-second turn timeout.
Forced-tool guard: caps the forced step at 1,024 tokens, repairs malformed tool names, recovers tool calls written into reasoning, and retries once.
Summary steps receive no tools, so the model must answer in text.
methodology.toolResults: Read-style Salesforce tools return fictional fixture JSON shaped like Salesforce agent results. The drafting tools (campaign brief, content, content section, preview refinement) are answered by one fixed reference model that stands in for the Marketing Cloud agent, so creative quality depends on what the orchestrator asked for and how it presents the result, not on a canned string. Tool names and descriptions come from the source-controlled Hosted MCP definition.

suites.label: Demo scenarios
suites.description: The use-case library prompts (including the weather-aware restaurant push campaign) plus a save request and a publish request, through the full pipeline.

suites.label: Routing through the pipeline
suites.description: The routing set through the full pipeline, as evaluators experience it.

suites.label: Routing by the model alone
suites.description: The same prompts with no policy or intent router, so the model alone chooses whether and which tool to call. This isolates model quality.

checks.label: Right tool
checks.definition: The first tool called is the expected one (or, for a planned scenario, the calls start with the full plan in order), or no tool is called when the request must not reach Salesforce.

checks.label: Answered
checks.definition: The turn ends with non-empty assistant text.

checks.label: No tool errors
checks.definition: No invalid tool calls, tool failures, or provider errors.

checks.label: No false write claims
checks.definition: The answer never says something was saved, published, sent, activated, attached, or created as a task.

checks.label: Graph-grounded
checks.definition: When a knowledge-graph or memory tool was called, every fictional graph entity the answer names (accounts, people, campaigns, segments, menu items, content) appears in what the turn's tools returned. Turns without a graph tool pass. Runs recorded before this check show no rate.

checks.label: Agent request grounded
checks.definition: When the turn asked the Marketing Cloud Campaign Creation agent for a brief after gathering context, the request names the brand, a menu item the tools returned, and the city or weather; a preview refinement names the saved Brief ID. Other turns pass. Runs recorded before this check show no rate.

limitations: Quality scores come from LLM judges, not customers. "Would act" is a judge answering as a written persona, so read it as a relative ranking between models, not a forecast of real click or order rates. The judges are two different model families, no model judges its own family, and the report shows how often the two agree; the judge is checked against hand-written strong, mediocre, and weak reference answers before a run is published.

The simulated Marketing Cloud agent is one fixed model. It holds the copy engine constant across contestants but is not the real Salesforce agent, so absolute copy quality here is not the production agent's.

Pricing is a snapshot of Cloudflare's list prices; a run's dollar figures move if Cloudflare reprices. Runs recorded before cost tracking were priced from stored token counts with all input billed at the uncached rate.
Runs recorded before quality scoring carry no quality scores or rubric criteria.
Tool results are fictional fixtures, not live Salesforce responses, so latency excludes Salesforce agent time.
Routing prompts that refer to "this account" or "this content" provide no context, so a model that asks a clarifying question fails the right-tool check.
Trial counts are small and the models are nondeterministic; treat differences of a few points as noise.
Kimi K2.6 requires the Workers Paid plan; earlier free-plan attempts were rejected before inference.

Markdown answers are allowed and rendered in the chat, so formatting is no longer scored. Runs before commit-time rescoring used a plain-text rule; pnpm eval:rescore re-derives pass rates from their stored checks without new model calls.

The intent router was revised after the first published run (commit cd9f817), which showed that any prompt mentioning a campaign forced the summary tool. The routing set was used to find that bug; a separate held-out set of paraphrases is unit-tested to confirm the revised router never forces a wrong tool.
methodology.costModel: Cost is tokens times Cloudflare's published Workers AI per-million-token rates (snapshot 2026-11-05); neurons are derived at $0.011 per 1,000. Cached input tokens are billed at the cached rate where the model has one. The report splits spend into the models under test, the judge panel, and the simulated agent. Policy-routed turns make no model call and cost nothing. These estimates are before account-level billing adjustments, including the daily free allocation. The frontier models require paid access.

Understandable but wordy or unevenly structured.
Well structured and appropriately brief.

Distinctly on-brand; memorable phrasing that a human copywriter would keep.

Cardivance carries an active **boxed warning**. All usable promotional content must include it, along with important safety information and full prescribing information.

---

**Usable claims**

**Claim:** *Reduced the risk of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization by 20% versus enalapril in HFrEF.*  
- **Verdict:** Usable  
- **Type:** Efficacy  
- **Indication:** Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction — **on label**  
- **Trial support:** **CARDIO-HF** (n=8,442); endpoint: cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization; 20% relative risk reduction versus enalapril (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.73 to 0.87)  
- **Approved content and MLR approvals:**  
  - Cardivance rep detail aid — **MLR-2026-0413**; approved 2026-06-12; expires 2027-06-12  
  - Cardivance HFrEF outcomes email — **MLR-2026-0412**; approved 2026-06-12; expires 2027-06-12  
  - Cardivance formulary value dossier — **MLR-2026-0420**; approved 2026-06-20; expires 2027-06-20  
- **Required safety information:** Cardivance boxed warning, important safety information, full prescribing information; adverse event reporting (for rep and email assets)

**Claim:** *The most common adverse reactions were hypotension, hyperkalemia, cough and dizziness.*  
- **Verdict:** Usable  
- **Type:** Safety  
- **Indication:** Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction — **on label**  
- **Trial support:** **CARDIO-HF** (same evidence path as above)  
- **Approved content and MLR approvals:**  
  - Cardivance rep detail aid — **MLR-2026-0413**; approved 2026-06-12; expires 2027-06-12  
  - Cardivance HFrEF outcomes email — **MLR-2026-0412**; approved 2026-06-12; expires 2027-06-12  
- **Required safety information:** Cardivance boxed warning, important safety information, full prescribing information; adverse event reporting

---

**Blocked claims — must not be used in promotion**

**Claim:** *Improves outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.*  
- **Verdict:** Blocked: not supportable as stated  
- **Why blocked:** Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is **not on the approved label** (only investigational). The supporting trial **CARDIO-PRESERVE** has no results yet, so there is no completed trial support.

- **Action:** This claim must not appear in promotional content until a completed trial supports it and the indication is on the approved label

## Glucora materials: compliance and consistency check

Short answer: **not fully compliant.** Two of three Aprimo assets are usable, and the claims themselves are approved — but one live HCP page and one email are running on an expired MLR approval. All three systems below are **mocked** views.

### Aprimo (assets) — 3 assets, 2 usable now

| Aprimo ID | Asset | MLR approval | Status | Usable now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| APR-498760 | Glucora HbA1c efficacy email | MLR-2026-0301 (exp. 2027-04-02) | Approved | Yes |
| APR-147947 | Glucora weight and HbA1c email | MLR-2025-0988 (exp. 2026-09-30) | Expired | No |
| APR-761687 | Glucora formulary value dossier | MLR-2026-0305 (exp. 2027-04-10) | Approved | Yes |

### Veeva Vault (claims library) — 2 claims, both Approved

- **CLM-58961** (`claim-glucora-a1c`): "Lowered HbA1c by 0.9 percentage points versus placebo at 26 weeks." Referenced to the GLUCO-CONTROL Phase 3 CSR (n=3120).
- **CLM-79738** (`claim-glucora-weight`): "Patients lost up to 3.4 kg while lowering HbA1c." Same CSR reference.

Both claims are substantiated by the same study result, so the claim layer itself is consistent.

### Drupal (HCP site) — 2 pages, 1 non-compliant

- **Node 1302** `/hcp/glucora/clinical-data` — published, MLR-2026-0301, Approved, compliant.
- **Node 1301** `/hcp/glucora/weight` — published, MLR-2025-0988, **Expired**, flagged non-compliant.

### Where the systems disagree

- **The weight story is approved as a claim but expired as an asset.** Vault says CLM-79738 is Approved; the only document Vault links it to is "Glucora weight and HbA1c email" under **MLR-2025-0988**, which is Expired in Aprimo. So the claim is fine in isolation, but nothing currently carries it with valid approval.
- **A live page sits behind that same expired approval.** Drupal node 1301 `/hcp/glucora/weight` is still published on MLR-2025-0988, matching Aprimo's expired asset APR-147947. This is the clearest compliance gap: an HCP-facing page live on lapsed MLR review.
- **Minor consistency note:** the Aprimo assets carry different safety-information bundles — APR-498760 includes ISI, prescribing information and adverse-events; APR-147947 and APR-761687 list a narrower set. Worth confirming the required bundle per channel and asset type rather than treating it as an error.

### What I'd check next

1. Re-approval or unpublishing for node 1301 `/hcp/glucora/weight`.
2. Replacement of APR-147947, or renewal of MLR-2025-0988, before the weight claim is used anywhere else.
3. Confirm the safety-information bundle expected on email vs. portal dossiers.
